This user guide describes how to set up the ADAR3000/3001-EVALZ evaluation
board for the ADAR3000 and ADAR3001, and how it connects to an
FPGA carrier. The ADAR3000 and ADAR3001 data sheets provide
additional information and should be consulted when using the evaluation
board.

The ADAR3000/3001-EVALZ carries the beamformer, with its RF inputs RFIN1 to
RFIN4 and RF outputs RFOUT1 to RFOUT4 on 2.92 mm connectors, as single-ended
50 Ω coplanar waveguides. It is controlled through the 120-pin SDP connector
P5. On the bench it is usually driven by an SDP-S controller board and

The evaluation board is supplied from two bench supplies, applied to the test
loops on the board:
|Rail|Test loops|Supply capability|Expected draw|
|1.2 V analog|Red `1P2V` to `AGND`|250 mA|128 mA ± 12 mA (ADAR3000), 110 mA ± 10 mA (ADAR3001)|
|1.8 V digital|Red `1P8V` to `DGND`|20 mA|7 mA ± 3 mA|

Set the jumpers as follows for control from an FPGA carrier:
|Header|Setting|Function|
|P8|Pin 1 to pin 2|Connects the chip’s internal 1.0 V LDO output. Required.|
|P9|Pin 1 to pin 2|Connects the chip’s internal 1.0 V LDO output. Required.|
|P4|Pin 1 to pin 2|Ties `RESET_N` (RSTB) to 1.8 V, as shipp

All control signals reach the device through the SDP connector P5. The logic
level on the SDP side is VIO, which the controller supplies on P5: 3.3 V from
an SDP-S, and the FMC `VADJ` rail through the SDP-I-FMC interposer. Two
level translators shift VIO to the device’s 1.8 V:

- U1 carries the SPI:

Through the interposer, VIO is the carrier’s FMC `VADJ` rail, which must be
at **1.8 V**. `VADJ` also supplies the FPGA I/O banks behind the FMC
connector; at 0 V no pin on that connector can drive, and the SDP side of the
level translators is unpowered.

This guide provides quick instructions on how to set up the
ADAR3000/3001-EVALZ on:

- ZCU102 on FMC HPC1, through the SDP-I-FMC interposer

The following files are needed:

- HDL boot file: `system_top.xsa`, built from the
  projects/adar3000/zcu102 HDL project
- no-OS project: projects/adar300x


Instructions on how to build them from source can be found here:

- ADAR300X no-OS Example Project. More no-OS build
  details at Xilinx Buil

- AMD Xilinx Vivado and Vitis 2025.1 (downloading Vitis from
  here
  will include Vivado as well)
- A UART terminal (PuTTY/Tera Term/Minicom, etc.), baud rate 115200 (8N1)
- For the IIO example, libiio 1.0.0 or later

- AMD Xilinx ZCU102 FPGA board and its power supply
- ADAR3000/3001-EVALZ evaluation board
- SDP-I-FMC interposer
- Two bench power supplies, see
  Power supply
- 2x Micro-USB cables, one for UART and one for JTAG


More details as to why you need these, can be found at
Prerequisites.

The IIO example serves the device over the same UART to libiio clients such as
`iio_info`, `iio_attr` and `iio_rwdev`. Build and flash the
`iio_example` variant, close the UART terminal, and check that the device
enumerates:

```bash
iio_info -u serial:/dev/ttyUSB0,115200,8n1
```
